data.narrative:
Enigma is a seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Jonathan Jacobi and Gal Niv, both former Unit 8200 operatives with prior experience at Microsoft and Check Point. The company has raised $71M to date. The relevant comp universe consists of nine private robotics firms (including Walden Robotics, Divergent, Exotec, Locus Robotics, and Generalist AI) and one public comparable.

Stage-progression methodology is the applicable valuation approach here. Using total capital raised of $71M as a proxy for current value and applying a 2.5x multiplier typical of seed-to-next-stage advancement yields an implied valuation of $178M. Peer-median triangulation cannot be reliably applied; while ten same-sector peers exist, the robotics and manufacturing universe lacks sufficient depth at Enigma's stage and valuation tier to support a statistically defensible comparable median. Narrowing to same-stage, adjacent-stage, or similar-tier peers yields fewer than three datapoints, making sector-wide aggregation inappropriate.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $151M to $204M, with a median point of $178M. This range reflects confidence in the stage-progression method applied to the $71M raised baseline, with the bounds capturing reasonable variance around the 2.5x multiplier. Key uncertainties include capital deployment efficiency post-seed, competitive positioning within an increasingly crowded robotics sector, and the substantive differentiation of the platform relative to the identified peer set. Limited public comparables further constrain precision.
